solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One detecting tail of carpet snake

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its very end, so only its final letter is kept

blocks.note: the last letter of carpet
a racer is a fast North American snake

explanation.surface: Someone spots the end of a snake poking out from under the rug.
explanation.definitionFit: A tracer is something that tracks or detects, such as a radioactive marker followed through a system.

clue.text: Respondent travelling via Crete

indicators.note: letters that are travelling move from their places into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone answering a survey while touring through Crete.
explanation.walkthrough: Respondent looks like a noun, a person answering, but it is used as the adjective meaning responding.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective respondent means responding to a stimulus, which is what reactive describes.

clue.text: Cheers double feature

blocks.note: a facial feature, the chin, written twice

explanation.surface: A toast raised at a cinema showing two films back to back.
explanation.walkthrough: Double feature means a cinema programme of two films; read cryptically, it is one facial feature written twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Chin-chin is an old-fashioned British drinking toast, the same as saying cheers.

clue.text: Bother cook with graduate job

blocks.note: to cook the books is to rig or falsify them
an MA is a Master of Arts graduate
a role is a job or position

explanation.surface: A cook fussing over a new graduate's job application.
explanation.walkthrough: Cook suggests the kitchen, but it means falsify, as in cooking the books.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigmarole is a tiresome, fussy procedure, which is a hassle or bother.

clue.text: Woolly tops of cabaret artistes dancing in drag

indicators.note: the tops of words are their opening letters, so each word gives only its first letter
letters that are dancing move about and end up in a new order

blocks.note: the first letters of cabaret and artistes
taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Cabaret performers in drag, dancing in their woolly tops.
explanation.walkthrough: Woolly reads as an adjective describing the tops, but it is the noun meaning a knitted garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Woolly is used as a noun for a knitted garment, and a cardigan is a buttoned knitted jacket.

clue.text: Acting on her suspicions and expertise

indicators.note: acting on something means working it over, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A detective who acts on her hunches, and has the know-how to back them.
explanation.definitionFit: Connoisseurship is the specialist knowledge and discerning judgement of a connoisseur, a form of expertise.

clue.text: Strip beside privet hedges

indicators.note: to hedge is to enclose, so the words enclose the answer within them

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of beside and most of privet

explanation.surface: A strip of land running beside some privet hedges.
explanation.walkthrough: Hedges looks like a plural noun completing the privet picture, but it is a verb meaning surrounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip someone of something is to take it away from them, which is what deprive means.

clue.text: Airmen able to stop half-cut lass writing on wall

indicators.note: cut in half means only one half of the word is left
to stop a gap is to plug it, so these letters go inside the other word

blocks.note: the RAF is the Royal Air Force
fit means able, as in fit to work
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: Pilots who can stop a drunken girl scrawling on the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: Half-cut is British slang for tipsy, but here it means cut in half: only the first two letters of the girl survive.
explanation.definitionFit: Graffiti is writing or drawings scrawled on a wall in a public place.

clue.text: Petty new leader eschewing laughter

indicators.note: eschewing means avoiding, so the word goes without its leading letter

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
giggling is laughter

explanation.surface: A trivial new boss who refuses to laugh.
explanation.definitionFit: Niggling describes something minor and fiddly, so it means trifling, the sense of petty.

clue.text: Understanding similar spirit after time

indicators.note: after says the following pieces come behind the abbreviation that ends the clue's phrase

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
akin means similar
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: Grasping a kindred spirit after some time has passed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after time' tells you the letter for time comes first: similar spirit follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking in something means absorbing or comprehending it, so it is a phrasal synonym of understanding.

clue.text: Emerged from second crash

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a prang is British slang for a minor car crash

explanation.surface: Someone climbed out of the wreckage a moment after a car accident.
explanation.definitionFit: To spring from a place or source is to arise or come out of it, as in sprang from nowhere.

clue.text: Clipped very accommodating pet backwards and forwards

indicators.note: read backwards, the word for a pet runs from its end to its start
a word accommodating others gives them room inside itself

blocks.note: so means very, as in so good
a cat is a pet, here read backwards
the same pet read the normal way round

explanation.surface: A very tolerant pet that will go backwards and forwards on command.
explanation.walkthrough: The pet appears twice, once backwards and once forwards, and both go inside the word for very.
explanation.definitionFit: Staccato describes notes or speech cut short and detached, which is what clipped means.

clue.text: Naughty fun is ultimately immoral and bad

indicators.note: ultimately points to the end of the word, so only the last letter is taken
bad letters are corrupted and out of their proper order

blocks.note: taken as written
the final letter of immoral

explanation.surface: A moralist's verdict that naughty fun is wicked in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Naughty can mean wicked or morally wrong, the older sense that sinful shares.

clue.text: Puritan press team

blocks.note: to iron clothes is to press them
a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: A puritanical group of journalists working together.
explanation.walkthrough: Press suggests newspapers, but it is the verb for smoothing clothes. Ironsides were Cromwell's Puritan cavalry in the English Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironside was the nickname of Oliver Cromwell and of his Puritan troopers, so it can denote a Puritan soldier.

clue.text: Sprightly old lady embraced by accomplished girl on farm

indicators.note: something embraced by another is held within its arms

blocks.note: airy means light and lively
your old lady is your mother, ma
did means accomplished, carried out

explanation.surface: A lively elderly woman hugged by a talented young farm girl.
explanation.walkthrough: Accomplished reads as an adjective praising the girl, but it is the past tense verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A dairymaid is a woman employed on a farm to milk cows and make butter and cheese.

clue.text: Joined in thread broadcast on radio

indicators.note: on the radio words are heard, not read, so only their sound counts

blocks.note: seed broadcast is scattered, or sown

explanation.surface: Something stitched into a thread of a broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: Broadcast looks like the radio theme, but here it means scattered like seed by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewn means stitched together with needle and thread, so it is a way of being joined.

clue.text: Spooner's gang collapsed in bar

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of neighbouring words

blocks.note: a gang is a band and collapsed is sank; Spooner swaps their opening sounds

explanation.surface: A gang of drinkers in the reverend's local pub.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the first sounds of band and sank gives the answer. Bar looks like a pub, but it is a ridge of sand in the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandbank is a raised ridge of sand in a river or the sea, also called a sandbar.

clue.text: Road with bend ahead in Lancaster?

indicators.note: ahead means in front, so this piece is placed before the other one

blocks.note: to warp is to bend out of shape
a lane is a road

explanation.surface: A warning sign of a curve ahead on a road in Lancaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with bend ahead' puts the bend before the road. Lancaster looks like the English city, but the question mark marks an example: the Avro Lancaster was a Second World War bomber.
explanation.definitionFit: The Avro Lancaster was a British heavy bomber, so it is an example of a military aircraft.

clue.text: Turn informer, regularly using espionage

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every second one is kept

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of espionage

explanation.surface: A spy who becomes an informer regularly uses espionage.
explanation.definitionFit: To sing is slang for confessing or informing to the police, like a canary.

clue.text: Vacuously silly subject entirely upended curriculum

indicators.note: emptied of contents, the word keeps only its outside letters
turned upside down in a down entry, the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the first and last letters of silly
sub, short for subordinate, is one subject to another
all means entirely, as in all alone

explanation.surface: A pointless subject turns a whole course of study upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: A syllabus is the outline of topics in a course, which is what a curriculum sets out.

clue.text: Problem of island swathed in shade

indicators.note: something swathed in material is wrapped up inside it

blocks.note: IS is an abbreviation for island
a nuance is a subtle shade of meaning or colour

explanation.surface: The trouble with an island lost in shadow.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuisance is an annoying thing or person, so it is a problem or bother.

clue.text: Dispatch star heartlessly

indicators.note: without a heart means the central letter of the word is removed

blocks.note: a star is a celebrity

explanation.surface: A famous person is sent off without mercy.
explanation.walkthrough: Dispatch reads as a verb, sending someone off, but it is the noun for speed, as in done with dispatch.
explanation.definitionFit: Celerity is swiftness of movement, which is the sense of dispatch meaning promptness.

clue.text: Nick grandad's last cabbage

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, the only one kept

blocks.note: to nick and to collar are both slang for arrest
the final letter of grandad

explanation.surface: Stealing the last of grandad's cabbages from his allotment.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick looks like steal, but it means arrest here; in British slang both nick and collar mean to arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: Collards are a loose-leaved variety of cabbage, often called collard greens.

clue.text: Spot papa parking in valley

indicators.note: in places these letters inside the word that follows

blocks.note: P is papa in the NATO alphabet
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
a dale is a valley

explanation.surface: Catching sight of Dad parking the car down in the valley.
explanation.definitionFit: To dapple is to mark with spots or patches, so it is a verb meaning to spot.

clue.text: Unknown soldiers returned with famous Cavalier

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so these letters are read from the end

blocks.note: y is an unknown quantity in algebra
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers
A-list means the most famous celebrities

explanation.surface: An Unknown Soldier is brought home alongside a celebrated Cavalier.
explanation.walkthrough: Cavalier looks like part of the military scene, and it is the definition: Cavaliers were the King's party in the English Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: Cavaliers fought for Charles I against Parliament, so a Cavalier is a supporter of the monarchy.

clue.text: Film average Gulf resident without clothes

indicators.note: stripped of clothes means the outer layer goes, so the first and last letters are dropped

blocks.note: AV is the abbreviation for average
a Qatari lives in the Gulf state of Qatar

explanation.surface: A film about an ordinary Gulf resident walking about naked.
explanation.definitionFit: Avatar is James Cameron's 2009 film, so the answer is an example of a film.

clue.text: Ecstasy in handbag strangely getting nod at rock concert?

indicators.note: in places one letter inside the following word
letters arranged strangely are out of their usual order

blocks.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
taken as written

explanation.surface: Drugs smuggled in a handbag at a rock concert.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: nodding hard to the beat at a rock gig.
explanation.definitionFit: To headbang is to shake the head violently in time to rock music, an extreme version of nodding along.

clue.text: Very involved in living without poverty

indicators.note: without here means outside, so one word wraps around the other

blocks.note: your keep is your living, what pays for your board
need means poverty, as in families in need

explanation.surface: Someone deeply engaged in a life free of poverty.
explanation.walkthrough: Without looks like it means lacking, but here it is the old sense of outside.
explanation.definitionFit: To be knee-deep in something is to be heavily immersed or embroiled in it.

clue.text: Report missing setter, lazy individual

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so one letter is taken out of the word

blocks.note: a dossier is a file or report
the setter refers to themself as I

explanation.surface: A report that the setter is a layabout has gone missing.
explanation.definitionFit: A dosser is British slang for an idler who avoids work, or someone who sleeps rough.
